It returns `needs_user` for login, MFA, CAPTCHA, or ambiguous capture. This worker is operationally conditional and has no live provider guarantee in the test suite.

### Cancellations and scheduler

`cancellations.py` is also evidence-first. A request is persisted and idempotent, transitions the subscription to `cancel_requested`, and refuses unsafe candidates/demo/sandbox cases. Completion requires provider-confirmed evidence with an HTTPS URL, nonempty text, a captured date, effective date, and matching receipt/browser evidence. Opening a provider page is not completion. Stale jobs recover, and worker readiness/handoff can pause for the user. The cancellation worker is optional and requires local Codex/Luna authentication; there is no API-key fallback.

`scheduler.py` keeps sync state per item and uses UTC for sync metadata while maintaining local-time rules for receipt attempt/stale logic. It reads a configured interval clamped to a safe range, skips items without tokens, serializes overlapping sync runs, and returns per-item failures without aborting all items. In tests (`LEDGER_TESTING`, `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`) it reports skipped rather than calling Plaid. Subscription scanning follows successful sync rather than running after a failed item indiscriminately. The server's production main loop may run scheduler and cancellation/receipt worker polling, while demo mode avoids real external actions.

### API reconstruction checklist

Implement the following route families with the guards above:

- `GET /api/health`, `/api/auth/status`, `/api/config`, `/api/accounts`, `/api/items`, `/api/categories`.
- `GET /api/transactions` with scope/account/category/search/date/limit/offset filters and receipt allocation search/category support; sort by posted date descending and insertion row order.
- `GET /api/summary/overview`, `/api/summary/networth`, `/api/summary/cashflow`, `/api/summary/categories`, `/api/summary/heatmap`, `/api/summary/matrix`, `/api/monthly-plan`, `/api/reports/spending`, `/api/projections/defaults`.
- `GET /api/budgets`, `/api/goals`, `/api/business/summary`, `/api/subscriptions`, `/api/cancellations`, `/api/receipts`, `/api/receipts/transaction?id=<transaction>`, and `/api/sync/status`.
- `GET /api/export/transactions.csv` with formula-injection-safe text and receipt allocation rows in place of the accepted parent charge when the allocation is valid.
- Auth mutations for setup/login/logout; config save; manual account/transaction/budget/goal mutations; subscription save/scan/review; projections; cancellation request/resume; receipt settings/request/resume/review/undo; sync.
- Plaid link token/exchange/sandbox-token have environment, auth, origin, and demo guards; item refresh and account classification/archive are authenticated/origin-checked HTTP mutations but are not all DEMO-only paths.
- Demo seed and data reset are authenticated HTTP actions, but the current routes are not explicitly DEMO-only: seed blocks replacing linked bank data, while reset blocks pending cancellation jobs and linked bank items. Preserve that distinction when reconstructing or hardening them.

Return validation failures as controlled 4xx responses. Do not allow provider exceptions, malformed receipt payloads, or database integrity errors to leak secrets or stack traces. Preserve compatibility fields such as subscription `monthly_cost` and receipt `can_apply` while adding newer review detail fields.

### Tests and verification plan

The source test suite is the reconstruction oracle. Run focused module tests first with the repository's import arrangement so `backend.db` is used rather than a globally installed package: `tests/test_finance.py` covers subscriptions and forecasts; `tests/test_plaid.py` covers exchange/refresh; `tests/test_reports.py` covers calendar/all-time reports; `tests/test_receipts.py` and `tests/test_receipt_invariants.py` cover exact receipt allocation; `tests/test_receipt_worker.py` covers worker validation/bridge; `tests/test_cancellations.py` covers evidence and idempotency; `tests/test_auth.py` covers sessions; `tests/test_integration.py` and `tests/test_receipt_api.py` cover server contracts.

Minimum regression cases are:

- `init_db()` and every workflow `init_schema()` are idempotent.
- Two Plaid exchanges for the same item preserve local item/account IDs. A supplied existing local item ID that mismatches the provider item fails without orphaning data.
- Modified Plaid rows preserve manually edited scope, transfer, category, and name while provider metadata changes.
- Archived accounts remain in Reports and all-time totals but cannot launch receipts or contribute active balances.
- December 31 belongs to its calendar year and January 1 to the next; leap-day February is counted; an empty year has twelve explicit zero months and null date coverage.
- Future posted rows, pending rows, transfers, and positive income/refunds are excluded from gross spend. A future transaction later within the current month remains excluded.
- Business-only and personal-only filters use effective transaction scope, including scope overrides.
- Month totals, category totals, and all-time/year totals reconcile exactly in cents.
- Irregular grocery, supermarket, gas, or dining charges never become active subscriptions; three exact SaaS monthly charges can become active; variable bills remain candidates or active with a price review, never silently changing or dropping the commitment.
- January 31 monthly anchors preserve their day intent through short months. Unsupported custom intervals are skipped rather than aborting scanning. A user-saved next due date resets the billing-day anchor when billing day was not explicitly supplied.
- One posted transaction can reconcile at most once in a monthly plan, including duplicate subscriptions or due events. Pending spend is exposed separately and paid/upcoming entries are sorted by due.
- Forecast defaults classify by account type, count negative balances as debt, retain positive credit/loan balances as assets, and preserve the balance identity. Debt uses nominal APR/12. Negative annual returns, including -99%, remain finite and real.
- Receipt exact cents reject malformed strings/floats/bools, unknown categories, null autoapply categories, overlong fields, excessive item counts, and mismatched totals. Wrong category-list length rejects review without applying. Corrected item categories preserve exact cents and replace only the category overlay.
- Receipt evidence requires a matching transaction currency and actual account mask for automatic application. Missing mask or missing Apple card data produces review. Same order cannot be applied to two charges. Dismissing a transaction releases its own reservation so it can be re-looked-up.
- Daily limits count failed attempts and resumed claims. Stale local-time jobs recover, and an old worker cannot finish a newer claim when `expected_attempt` differs.
- Undo restores the saved parent category state and removes the display allocation overlay, so the parent name/category fallback is shown again. A Plaid financial fingerprint change invalidates accepted allocations and falls back to the parent transaction.
- Config responses expose independent saved flags and never raw secrets. Empty credential saves preserve prior credentials. Link flow fetches fresh config rather than trusting stale frontend state.

Use isolated temporary `LEDGER_DATA_DIR` directories for every test. Do not call live Plaid, Amazon, Apple, Google, or cancellation providers. Tests should use provider-shaped fixtures and monkeypatched network seams. A full-suite pass is useful only after focused tests pass because concurrent agents or import path collisions can otherwise mask domain failures.

### Actual limitations and non-goals

The application is not a bank ledger with double-entry reconciliation. Account balances are provider/manual snapshots plus transaction mutations; historical net worth is reconstructed approximately. SQLite `REAL` compatibility rows mean old data may carry fractional-cent artifacts even though new reports quantize cents. There is no market feed, tax filing model, investment lot accounting, or guaranteed forecast accuracy.

Plaid requires valid environment-specific credentials and an exact HTTPS redirect URL configured in the provider dashboard for production. Sandbox and demo paths are intentionally constrained. Scheduler state is local and per item; a process crash can leave work to be recovered by stale windows. External provider errors are mapped safely but cannot be made reliable by this code alone.

Receipt lookup does not read email, scrape purchases, process refunds, or mutate merchant orders. It can identify Amazon/Apple/Google candidates and propose item descriptions/categories, but evidence verification and user interaction are required for uncertain captures. Receipt splits are overlays, so consumers that bypass `allocation_map()` will see the parent category; every spending consumer must use the effective allocation helper to remain coherent. Accepted receipt descriptions are display overlays and should not overwrite the bank's base name.

Cancellation automation is evidence-dependent and browser-dependent. A worker can pause for login/MFA/CAPTCHA or user confirmation. A URL or page opening without visible provider-confirmed evidence must never mark a cancellation complete. The system is single-owner and designed for a private deployment; multi-user authorization, sharing, and role-based access are outside the pinned implementation.

Configuration redaction means “saved” is not “validated.” The local database and JSON configuration are protected by file permissions but are not an encrypted secrets vault. Backups must therefore be protected separately. The standard deployment guidance uses a dedicated non-login user, a mode-700 data directory, loopback binding/Tailscale or an equivalent private network, and online SQLite backups; public exposure is outside the safe default.

### Suggested independent remake milestones

First, reproduce database creation and the deterministic tests for signs, scopes, archived history, and reports. Next, reproduce account/transaction mutations and manual override persistence, then add Plaid-shaped refresh fixtures. Add subscriptions only after exact identity and due matching are tested. Add forecasts with numerical invariant tests. Implement receipts as a closed local state machine with exact cents and fingerprints before connecting a worker. Implement cancellation state/evidence separately. Finally wire the guarded HTTP routes and web display overlays.

At each milestone, treat the database row and its transition rules as the contract. Do not let a UI label such as “active,” “Saved,” “Verified,” or “Canceled” stand in for a state transition: active subscriptions need lifecycle state; saved Plaid fields need independent booleans; verified receipt captures need evidence checks; canceled jobs need provider-confirmed evidence. Keep all provider calls behind explicit environment gates and test seams. This ordering yields a deterministic private finance core even when Plaid, browser automation, or user approval is unavailable.


## 8. Exact reconstruction procedure for a new Luna session

### 8.1 Choose a new destination separate from live data

Restore into an empty working directory such as `Ledger-rebuilt`. Do not extract over a live data directory, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\LedgerPersonal`, a deployment directory, or another Git checkout with unrelated work. The extractor refuses an existing destination so a typo does not overwrite records. This is a new code copy with no financial data or secrets.

There are two equivalent source recovery paths:

- Extract the companion `Ledger-Source.zip`. It contains a top-level `Ledger/` directory.
- Run the companion `RESTORE-LEDGER-SOURCE.py` against this Markdown file. It recreates every embedded source file and checks SHA256 before writing. The full extractor is also printed below so the Markdown alone is sufficient to recover application source and binary assets.

On macOS/Linux, using Python 3.11 or newer:

```bash
python3 RESTORE-LEDGER-SOURCE.py \
  'LEDGER — COMPLETE BUILD AND LIGHT MODE RECONSTRUCTION.md' \
  /tmp/Ledger-rebuilt
cd /tmp/Ledger-rebuilt
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Use a real writable new directory if `/tmp/Ledger-rebuilt` already exists. Do not remove an existing directory just to satisfy the example. On Windows use `py -3` or the bundled Python executable where appropriate. Desktop-specific tests include portable checks; the native Windows UI has to be assessed on Windows.

A fully restored tracked-source tree has the same bytes as the included snapshot, not necessarily a `.git` directory. Git history is not needed to run the application. If version control is desired, initialize a new repository after extraction or clone the original repository and check out the included snapshot. The public repository is an alternate retrieval route, not a runtime dependency of the finance app.

### 8.2 Create an isolated light-mode reference instance

The default config already selects `theme: light`, `palette: paper`, `font_family: lora`, `accent: blue`, `density: comfortable`. A previous browser's localStorage may briefly affect appearance before saved config is loaded. Use a fresh browser context, or choose Light / Warm newsprint / Lora explicitly in Settings. Do not change live preferences just to take a reference screenshot.

Start a dedicated synthetic preview:

```bash
LEDGER_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ledger-light-reference-data \
LEDGER_DEMO=1 LEDGER_TESTING=1 LEDGER_PORT=18937 \
python3 backend/server.py
```

Use a NEW data directory for that preview. Open `http://127.0.0.1:18937/`. Sample mode deliberately bypasses the ordinary single-owner setup and disables real bank linking and agent dispatch. The ordinary app without `LEDGER_DEMO=1` prompts for owner setup through localhost. Use Settings → Sample data & reset → Load samples when appropriate in the isolated preview; do not reset a live database. The fixture generator is in `backend/seed_demo.py`, so the exact sample categories/accounts/transactions are recoverable from source. The fixture dates may be generated relative to runtime; differences in a screenshot's month or values do not justify altering the visual design.

The browser URLs are hash routes (`#overview`, `#transactions`, etc.). The HTTP server must serve the frontend and API together. Opening `web/index.html` directly with `file://` is not a working reconstruction: the app depends on `/api` routes, same-origin cookies, and absolute stylesheet/script paths.

For a reference clone, do not connect banks or enable worker lookups to populate it. Sample/manual test records are sufficient to exercise layouts, financial totals, reports, review drawers, and projections. This avoids confusing live personal state with reproducible design evidence.

### 8.3 Inspect the shell before changing anything

The HTML root must resolve to `data-theme="light"`, `data-palette="paper"`, and `data-font="lora"`. Load every stylesheet and script in exactly the order in `web/index.html`. This is important because the application evolved by replacing some original page renderers and extending the CSS cascade. Correct files in the wrong order can produce the old UI even when each file seems valid independently.

Check the logo, cream paper, sidebar width, active tab, fine top/header dividers, overview greeting/subheader, and three lead cards before assessing inner pages. Set the viewport first; desktop expanded, desktop collapsed, and mobile drawer are intentionally different layouts. A good desktop comparison size is 1440×900; repeat around 1280×800 and 390×844. These sizes are suggested test viewports, not hidden source constants.

### 8.4 Incremental rebuilding if source reuse is intentionally forbidden

If someone specifically asks to implement from scratch rather than restore the provided source, work in this dependency order:

1. Implement SQLite schema, config loading/saving/redaction, server routing, input validation, auth, and health endpoint.
2. Implement categories/accounts/transaction CRUD and the sign/scope/transfer invariants. Add tests before building financial summaries.
3. Build the frontend shell, exact light tokens, fonts, logo, responsive sidebar, modal behavior, form error states, and the shared API helper.
4. Implement the monthly plan and summary APIs, then Home cards and quick entry. Confirm zero-data and over-budget states.
5. Implement transaction list filters, category changes, scope/transfer overrides, and exports. Confirm add/edit/delete effects on manual balances.
6. Implement budgets/goals/personal/business and reports. Reconcile month, year, all-time, and category totals using one synthetic fixture.
7. Implement subscription normalization, candidates, price reviews, due-date/cadence handling, and monthly reconciliation. Test expected versus paid counts.
8. Implement projections and chart rendering with deterministic formula tests.
9. Implement Plaid configuration, Link, exchange, cursor sync, update-mode relinking, environmental restrictions, and OAuth resumption. Use mocks until explicitly authorized bank setup is available.
10. Implement cancellation queue/worker/protocol/evidence validation and human handoff. Do not equate an agent narrative with verified cancellation.
11. Implement receipt queue/provider bridge/evidence validation/category allocations/review/undo and preservation of manual choices. Test that itemization never duplicates the bank transaction amount.
12. Package the Python server and frontend for Ubuntu/Docker and Windows, preserving independent data directories. Add only the startup/runtime components needed for each platform.
13. Compare all visible states against the light-mode specification and use the complete embedded source to resolve ambiguity.

This order reduces the temptation to implement the same accounting logic separately in every UI page. The final interface must reflect backend truth rather than calculating invented totals in the browser.

## 9. Ubuntu and private remote operation

### 9.1 Minimal runtime

Core Ledger uses Python's standard library: HTTP server, SQLite, JSON, dates, threading, cryptography primitives available in the standard library, subprocess control, and urllib for Plaid. There is no required React/Vite/Next build and no required Python package install for ordinary manual finance tracking. `requirements.txt` documents this minimal runtime. Node dependencies are for the optional local browser/Codex tooling, not for rendering the dashboard or storing a manual transaction.

For a personal non-container service, the included `scripts/install-ubuntu.sh` installs code separately from data, uses a dedicated service account, and provides systemd units. Its update mode preserves the data directory and service environment. Use its documented dry-run before adapting paths. Adapt the source and data paths to your own installation.

### 9.2 Docker invariants

The repository Dockerfile pins a Node 22 Bookworm base by digest and installs Python, CA certificates, tini, time zone data, the pinned npm dependencies, and Chromium with required OS libraries. It runs as UID/GID 1000. The compose configuration uses a read-only application filesystem, dropped Linux capabilities, no-new-privileges, `/tmp` tmpfs, and persistent `/var/lib/ledger`. Host publication is loopback-only. The app may bind `0.0.0.0` inside its container to support the mapping, but that is not permission to expose it on all host interfaces.

The dedicated writable data volume contains the database, app config, optional worker profiles/authentication, and job workspaces. `.dockerignore` excludes data/config/env files, databases, browser-related state, node_modules from the source context, archives, and caches. A source export is not a backup of records. A data backup is not an application source export.

The container healthcheck calls the local `/api/health`. Its result can establish that the HTTP process responds; it cannot establish bank synchronization, correct external credentials, merchant authentication, or whether a cancellation actually completed.

### 9.3 Initial owner password from another computer

Initial setup is restricted to localhost. From an authorized remote computer, use SSH forwarding to reach your server through a local address while preserving authentication and the first-setup restriction. The user enters their own password in the UI. Once set, authentication is preserved in the database. Future updates do not recreate the password or send it through tools.

A generic example is:

```bash
ssh -N -L 18917:127.0.0.1:8907 your-user@your-tailnet-host
```

If the client computer is on another network, a LAN address alone is not sufficient; connect both machines through your private network or other intentionally configured routing.

### 9.4 Permanent address and bank-return origin

Use the private HTTPS Ledger URL when linking banks. The frontend stores the temporary Link token and scope in sessionStorage for OAuth return. SessionStorage is scoped to browser origin. Starting at `http://127.0.0.1:18917` and returning to `https://…:8443` loses the original sessionStorage context. The new `startLinkFlow()` origin guard detects this and offers the configured Ledger address before initiating the flow. It does not move session cookies or bank tokens between origins.

Plaid's project/website field and OAuth redirect setting are different. A GitHub repository can describe the project; it cannot resume Ledger's OAuth session. Each user must configure an appropriate return address for their own installation if the bank flow requires it. The Windows package contains no private server configuration and does not proxy to another person's server.

### 9.5 Safe update and rollback pattern

Compare the proposed source with your currently deployed version. Back up source and deployment configuration, build the new image successfully, and then update only the Ledger service. Preserve custom GUI/worker layers where present; the generic container definition may not include locally added services. Keep the data volume in place and verify authentication after restarting.

The saved-key patch affects `backend/db.py`, `backend/plaid_client.py`, `web/app2.js`, `web/comfort.js` and `web/comfort.css`, with supporting tests. Keep the corresponding tests with the source.

If performing a future rollback, inspect current schema changes first. This specific patch added config response flags and frontend/error guidance without a new database schema migration, but future patches may differ. Restoring an old image does not undo a data migration automatically. Use recorded backups intentionally and do not restore live data just to revert a CSS change.

## 10. Windows desktop application

### 10.1 What “desktop application” means here

The package runs the same private Python HTTP server and web UI on the user's Windows computer. The launcher opens Edge in app-window mode when available and uses the default browser otherwise. It is a desktop convenience wrapper around the same app, not Electron, a rewritten GUI, a public website, or an offline mobile application. No terminal command must be pasted for ordinary launch/update use.

The distribution includes CPython 3.13.15's official Windows x64 embeddable ZIP, licensed by Python's included license. Provenance URL:

`https://www.python.org/ftp/python/3.13.15/python-3.13.15-embed-amd64.zip`

Original runtime SHA256:

`d1f04d990aee1253d8569e8e5104e30fa9f5fa830899f14843448872d936a2cf`

The builder verifies that digest and modifies only `python313._pth` to include the application paths:

```text
python313.zip
.
../desktop/windows
../app/backend
```

These pins record the runtime used in this release. A future maintainer should review newer runtime releases deliberately instead of changing the download URL without updating verification. The runtime binary itself is not embedded in the Markdown appendix; it is included in the companion ready-made Windows ZIP, and can otherwise be downloaded from the pinned official URL.

### 10.2 Directory layout

The extracted distribution has a top-level `Ledger-Desktop-Windows/` folder containing:

```text
INSTALL-LEDGER.cmd
READ-ME.txt
RUNTIME-PROVENANCE.txt
PACKAGE-MANIFEST.sha256
ledger.ico
runtime/
  python.exe
  pythonw.exe
  python313.zip
  python313._pth
  ...official runtime files...
app/
  backend/
  web/
  scripts/
  ...source and source instructions...
desktop/windows/
  install.py
  launcher.py
  server_host.py
  win_ui.py
```

Installed program versions go under:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LedgerDesktop\versions\<timestamp-and-random-suffix>`

The private financial data path remains:

`%LOCALAPPDATA%\LedgerPersonal`

Data and program directories must stay separate. The installer creates a fresh staging/version directory rather than overwriting a running installed version. Older program versions are retained. It excludes private runtime names and symlinks from copying. It creates shortcuts using Windows shell-known Desktop and Programs locations, supporting redirected/OneDrive desktop folders rather than guessing a path under USERPROFILE.

The root CMD script uses `%~dp0`, disables delayed expansion, and quotes paths. These details avoid failures for spaces and special characters in a downloaded folder path. The installer needs no administrator account. It does not install a Windows service, change another Python installation, or add startup-at-login behavior.

### 10.3 Launcher lifecycle

A named per-data-directory instance lock prevents repeated launches from starting competing servers against one database. A second launch signals the existing supervisor to reopen the window. The Stop Ledger shortcut signals the same instance, waits for completion, and reports a confirmation. Closing the browser window itself leaves the server available in the background for fast reopening; stopping/restarting Windows stops it normally.

The supervisor uses `pythonw.exe` to remain hidden, but launches its child server with `python.exe` and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. This was an intentional correction: the console interpreter reliably supports redirected stdin for graceful shutdown while remaining invisible. The supervisor writes a private stop command through that pipe; it terminates only its own child on timeout. It does not kill an arbitrary process merely because port 8907 is occupied.

Before starting, it checks that port 8907 is free and validates the selected existing data directory. A damaged/unexpected data folder causes a visible error instead of silently importing or replacing records. Health readiness includes a newly generated desktop-instance identity so the launcher cannot accidentally accept another HTTP service as its own child. Child environment construction strips inherited Ledger/Plaid/Codex/OpenAI/Anthropic variables before supplying its deliberate local settings; this avoids inheriting the sender's or another shell's service configuration.

The local log is `LedgerPersonal\desktop.log`, rotated at its configured size threshold. Logs are private operational state, not content to upload routinely. The window uses the server's owner login. An installed program update does not require a new owner password if existing data is selected correctly.

### 10.4 Updating without commands

Update instructions:

1. Use **Stop Ledger** and wait for it to finish. Close the old Ledger window.
2. Obtain `Ledger-Desktop-Windows.zip` from this bundle. Right-click it and choose **Extract All**.
3. Open the extracted folder, double-click **INSTALL-LEDGER**, and choose **Yes** to open Ledger.

This is a clickable package with a short extraction step. It is not a one-click background auto-updater, an automatic update check inside Ledger, a signed MSI, or a signed EXE. Opening a download link does not silently install software.

The instructions do not ask users to disable Windows protections. The package is unsigned; native Windows trust dialogs were not exercised by the portable packaging checks.

### 10.5 Rebuilding the Windows package from this record

The shareable source's `desktop/build_windows.py` pins the sanitized `Ledger-Portable-Source.zip` digest. The companion `BUILD-WINDOWS-PACKAGE.py` verifies that archive and the official Python runtime before invoking the builder. It adds update instructions and produces a new runtime-provenance file and package manifest. Do not bypass input checksum verification.

Use `--restored-source` for the complete recovered source directory, `--portable-source` for `Ledger-Portable-Source.zip`, `--runtime` for the official runtime ZIP and `--output` for a new distribution filename. Consult `ARTIFACTS.sha256` for current companion checksums. The generic portable source notes are named `START-HERE.txt`; no recipient-specific instructions are included.

Portable tests exercised the actual package installation in an isolated temporary LOCALAPPDATA directory with sentinel database/settings/login files and an older version. The sentinel bytes and old version remained unchanged, the new source arrived, and the runtime executable had the expected Windows PE signature. These are useful packaging checks, but they do not claim that Edge shortcuts, native mutexes, download UX or Windows policy dialogs were exercised on a physical Windows laptop.

## 11. Optional workers: operational truth and cost boundary

The app source implements local cancellation and purchase-detail workers. To enable these optional integrations, a Codex CLI installation and your own supported ChatGPT-authenticated sign-in must exist under the service's dedicated identity and CODEX_HOME. An API-key login is not an authorized fallback in this project. The model is requested by the configured Luna identifier; availability, account limits, and future model naming are external conditions that the app does not guarantee.

Merchant/browser authentication is separate from the finance app's owner login and separate from your normal desktop browser. A worker profile on the home lab must actually be signed in to the relevant provider. The app can pause for a user, but cannot fabricate MFA, solve account terms by assumption, or call a cancellation completed just because it sent an instruction to an agent.

Check worker status and complete your own sign-in before enabling automation. Source code alone does not establish that a merchant or Codex account is authenticated.

The worker browser bridges have distinct scopes. The receipt bridge reads purchase information and does not purchase/refund/cancel orders. The cancellation bridge operates only for a user-requested cancellation. They share profile locking so a live user handoff and an automated worker do not race the same browser profile. Job attempt identity and evidence checks prevent old results from being applied to a newer attempt or changed transaction.

Keep account-specific service setup outside the portable app. Sharing source does not share banking or agent access. Core manual tracking requires no paid AI service; optional provider services can have separate costs. Decide those costs before enabling them.

## 12. Backups and restores

The included backup utility uses SQLite's online backup API to produce a consistent database snapshot. It stages an archive containing only `ledger.db` and, if present, `config.json`, then encrypts it through OpenSSL AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2, salt, and 600,000 iterations. The passphrase is supplied through stdin/file descriptor or a separately configured file, not command-line text. Encrypted staging is created on the destination filesystem so final rename does not cross filesystems.

The default backup path must be an actual mounted external filesystem unless an explicit local-backup option is used. This protects against accidentally filling the home-lab SSD when an expected external disk is absent. Restore validates archive members, duplicate names, required database presence, and SQLite integrity before replacing data, retaining a pre-restore recovery copy. It does not extract arbitrary archive paths into the system.

This describes the implemented utility and tests. A functioning backup script does not establish that scheduled backup and restore are configured on your machine. Do not mark that operational milestone complete merely because scripts and timers exist. The app data backup excludes optional Codex auth and merchant browser profiles; recovery of those integrations requires separate protected operational handling or fresh sign-ins. Never include them in a shareable source package.

For a local desktop installation, stop Ledger before copying the entire `LedgerPersonal` directory. Local data is not automatically synchronized to any server. A shared source folder is not a database backup.

## 14. Known boundaries and future work that should not be invented as complete

There is no implemented shared-couple ledger, multi-owner access control, shared household budget synchronization, automatic end-to-end encrypted device sync, universal automated cancellation guarantee, email-receipt ingestion, investment holding performance feed, or automatic Windows self-update service in this snapshot. Do not add these claims to the README or handoff because they sound like reasonable finance-app features.

The design and product requirements are fully described here. Reconstructing the app requires no private conversation history, personal memory or unrelated notes.

Plaid approval, product eligibility, supported institutions, Codex model availability, and provider account state can change. The documented settings show what was implemented and what succeeded in the documented implementation; future external setup must be verified on the relevant account. The app's “Saved” indicator deliberately states storage, not credential validation. If a provider requests a project description, describe your own use accurately. This guide does not guarantee provider approval.

The generic source includes optional Linux-oriented browser-worker mechanisms such as file locking/process group management. The Windows distribution provides the ordinary local finance app and launcher; it does not promise that the Linux browser-agent service stack is portable to Windows without separate work.

If using Luna for reconstruction, review its completed work against this guide. Use concrete, bounded subtasks and integrate reviewed results. The goal is a robust app with a quiet dashboard; it is not to maximize the number of panels, infrastructure services, or AI features.

## 15. Self-contained source extraction

The extractor below reads the exact file records in the appendix, rejects unsafe paths/duplicates, decodes binary assets, validates every SHA256 and byte count, then writes a fresh source directory. It does not connect to GitHub, read secrets, initialize a live database, or change a running application. Executable modes from Git are restored where the OS supports them. If a code block was edited or a Base64 blob damaged while syncing, it fails before writing the destination.


```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recover the pinned Ledger source from its self-contained Markdown manual."""
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import re

RECORD = re.compile(
    r'^<!-- LEDGER_SOURCE (\{[^\r\n]+\}) -->\n'
    r'(?P<fence>`{12,})(?:[a-z0-9_-]+)?\n'
    r'(?P<payload>.*?)\n(?P=fence)\n<!-- END_LEDGER_SOURCE -->',
    re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
)


def extract(manual, destination, with_mobile=False):
    destination = Path(destination)
    if destination.exists() or destination.is_symlink():
        raise ValueError('Destination must be a new directory; existing files will not be overwritten.')
    text = Path(manual).read_bytes().decode('utf-8')
    parsed = []
    seen = set()
    for match in RECORD.finditer(text):
        meta = json.loads(match.group(1))
        name = meta['path']
        path = PurePosixPath(name)
        if (path.is_absolute() or '..' in path.parts or '\\' in name or ':' in name
                or not path.parts or path.parts[0] == '.git' or name in seen):
            raise ValueError('Unsafe or duplicate source path: ' + name)
        seen.add(name)
        payload = match.group('payload')
        if meta['encoding'] == 'base64':
            data = base64.b64decode(''.join(payload.split()), validate=True)
        elif meta['encoding'] == 'utf-8':
            data = payload.encode('utf-8')
        else:
            raise ValueError('Unknown encoding: ' + name)
        if len(data) != meta['bytes'] or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != meta['sha256']:
            raise ValueError('Content check failed: ' + name)
        parsed.append((path, data, int(meta['mode'], 8)))
    if len(parsed) != 75:
        raise ValueError(f'Expected 75 source records; found {len(parsed)}. The manual may be incomplete.')
    if with_mobile:
        mobile_record = re.compile(RECORD.pattern.replace('LEDGER_SOURCE', 'LEDGER_MOBILE_SOURCE'), RECORD.flags)
        expected = {'web/index.html', 'web/mobile.css', 'web/mobile.js', 'web/manifest.json',
                    'web/apple-touch-icon.png', 'web/icon-192.png', 'web/icon-512.png',
                    'web/comfort.js', 'tests/test_finance.py'}
        overlay = {}
        for match in mobile_record.finditer(text):
            meta = json.loads(match.group(1))
            name = meta['path']
            if name not in expected or name in overlay:
                raise ValueError('Unexpected or duplicate mobile source: ' + name)
            payload = match.group('payload')
            if meta['encoding'] == 'base64':
                data = base64.b64decode(''.join(payload.split()), validate=True)
            elif meta['encoding'] == 'utf-8':
                data = payload.encode('utf-8')
            else:
                raise ValueError('Unknown mobile encoding: ' + name)
            if len(data) != meta['bytes'] or hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != meta['sha256']:
                raise ValueError('Mobile content check failed: ' + name)
            overlay[name] = (PurePosixPath(name), data, int(meta['mode'], 8))
        if set(overlay) != expected:
            raise ValueError('Expected all nine update source records.')
        combined = {str(path): (path, data, mode) for path, data, mode in parsed}
        combined.update(overlay)
        parsed = list(combined.values())
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    for path, data, mode in parsed:
        target = destination.joinpath(*path.parts)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        target.write_bytes(data)
        if os.name != 'nt':
            target.chmod(mode & 0o777)
    print(f'Restored and SHA256-verified {len(parsed)} files into {destination.resolve()}')
    return len(parsed)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('manual', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('destination', type=Path)
    parser.add_argument('--with-mobile', action='store_true', help='Apply the verified phone-layout and home-screen overlay')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    extract(args.manual, args.destination, with_mobile=args.with_mobile)
```

### Windows release build recipe

Save this as `BUILD-WINDOWS-PACKAGE.py` if the companion script is unavailable. Supply the restored application directory, the verified companion portable source ZIP, the official runtime ZIP, and a new output filename. ZIP timestamps can change the overall rebuilt archive digest; the source digest, runtime provenance and per-file manifest are the content-level checks.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the shareable Windows package using sanitized source and the official runtime."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util

SOURCE_SHA256 = 'f176ce5dcb2db70a82a8cb659eb370083dcfe927fedc55785e756b5bb78406c8'
RUNTIME_SHA256 = 'd1f04d990aee1253d8569e8e5104e30fa9f5fa830899f14843448872d936a2cf'
p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
p.add_argument('--restored-source', type=Path, required=True)
p.add_argument('--portable-source', type=Path, required=True)
p.add_argument('--runtime', type=Path, required=True)
p.add_argument('--output', type=Path, required=True)
a = p.parse_args()
for path, digest in [(a.portable_source, SOURCE_SHA256), (a.runtime, RUNTIME_SHA256)]:
    if hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != digest:
        raise SystemExit('Checksum mismatch: ' + str(path))
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('ledger_windows_build', a.restored_source / 'desktop/build_windows.py')
builder = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(builder)
builder.SOURCE_SHA256 = SOURCE_SHA256
builder.GUIDE = builder.GUIDE.replace('Install once\n', 'Update your existing Ledger\n1. Use the Stop Ledger shortcut and wait for it to finish. Close the old Ledger window.\n2. Extract this downloaded ZIP (right-click, Extract All).\n3. In the extracted folder, double-click INSTALL-LEDGER and choose Yes to open Ledger.\nYour existing records, password, bank credentials, and older installed version are kept.\n\nWhat changed in this update\nSaved Plaid keys now show masked dots and a Saved checkmark. Editing a key shows\nUnsaved. Bank setup errors give clearer guidance, and bank linking checks the\nlatest saved settings. Your own Plaid account and bank sign-in are still required\nfor automatic syncing; manual tracking works without them.\n\nFirst installation\n').replace('Right-click Ledger-Desktop-Windows.zip', 'Right-click the downloaded Ledger ZIP')
print(builder.build(a.portable_source, a.runtime, a.output))
```

### Source: `Dockerfile`

<!-- LEDGER_SOURCE {"path":"Dockerfile","bytes":2769,"sha256":"801aff3ce421191b3acc3e5840fdddf338c18670d1c4e99896946e11eba50540","encoding":"utf-8","mode":"644"} -->
````````````text
FROM node:22-bookworm-slim@sha256:83f487e0a63425e5b4d146fb5e5be574bcbe1b7b843d3ebafdd95eaf7767a7e5

# The image contains the stdlib Python server and the pinned Microsoft
# Playwright MCP package.  Playwright's own installer supplies Chromium and
# the Debian runtime libraries; no host browser or privileged container is
# required.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    NPM_CONFIG_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=false \
    TZ=America/Los_Angeles \
    PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update \
    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates python3 tini tzdata \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund \
    && test -f /app/node_modules/playwright-core/cli.js \
    && node /app/node_modules/playwright-core/cli.js install-deps chromium \
    && node /app/node_modules/playwright-core/cli.js install --no-shell chromium \
    && chmod -R a+rX /ms-playwright

COPY backend/ /app/backend/
COPY scripts/ /app/scripts/
COPY web/ /app/web/

# UID/GID 1000 is deliberate: the compose file uses the same non-root
# identity for the persistent data volume on the home lab. The official Node
# image already has UID/GID 1000 (`node`), so create a named account only when
# the base image does not provide one.
RUN if ! getent group 1000 >/dev/null; then groupadd --gid 1000 ledger; fi \
    && if ! getent passwd 1000 >/dev/null; then useradd --uid 1000 --gid 1000 --create-home --home-dir /var/lib/ledger --shell /usr/sbin/nologin ledger; fi \
    && existing_user="$(getent passwd 1000 | cut -d: -f1)" \
    && usermod --home /var/lib/ledger --shell /usr/sbin/nologin "$existing_user" \
    && mkdir -p /var/lib/ledger \
    && chown 1000:1000 /var/lib/ledger

ENV HOME=/var/lib/ledger \
    PATH=/app/node_modules/.bin:$PATH \
    CODEX_HOME=/var/lib/ledger/.codex \
    LEDGER_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/ledger \
    LEDGER_PORT=8907 \
    LEDGER_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0 \
    LEDGER_CODEX_CLI=/app/node_modules/.bin/codex \
    LEDGER_BROWSER_BRIDGE=/app/scripts/cancellation-browser.mjs \
    LEDGER_PLAYWRIGHT_MCP_CLI=/app/node_modules/@playwright/mcp/cli.js \
    LEDGER_BROWSER_WORKSPACE=/var/lib/ledger/cancellation-workspaces \
    LEDGER_BROWSER_PROFILE=/var/lib/ledger/browser-profile \
    LEDGER_CANCELLATION_WORK_DIR=/var/lib/ledger/cancellation-workspaces \
    LEDGER_BROWSER_HEADLESS=1

USER 1000:1000
EXPOSE 8907
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/tini", "--"]
CMD ["python3", "/app/backend/server.py"]

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=5 \
  CMD python3 -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8907/api/health', timeout=3)"
````````````

<!-- LEDGER_SOURCE {"path":"README.md","bytes":5349,"sha256":"ed3f316c38bc4d1cca333d5ca1e68b2cc83d54217ec1e5b68a188562132a2d6e","encoding":"utf-8","mode":"644"} -->
````````````text
# Ledger

A private finance dashboard for everyday spending, subscriptions, and the future you are planning. Built on the original Ledger.zip foundation with vanilla JavaScript, Python's standard library, SQLite, and locally bundled fonts.

The default appearance uses creamy paper surfaces, Lora headings, green and blue financial text, and warm copper details. Light, dark, and system modes are available. Settings also offers a colorful palette, font choices, spacing, and a simpler or fuller home layout.

## Start locally

Python 3.11 or newer is sufficient for manual tracking and the dashboard:

```bash
python3 backend/server.py
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8907/> and create your owner password. Your data stays in `backend/data/` unless `LEDGER_DATA_DIR` points elsewhere. Keep data outside the source directory for a permanent installation.

For a separate preview with synthetic data and bank/cancellation actions disabled:

```bash
LEDGER_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ledger-demo LEDGER_DEMO=1 LEDGER_PORT=18907 python3 backend/server.py
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:18907/>. Use a dedicated demo directory; sample data must not mix with real bank data.

## What is included

- A home dashboard with monthly spending, pending and expected charges, net worth, recent activity, upcoming payments, and quick transaction entry.
- Manual accounts and transactions; account balances update when manual transactions are entered or deleted. Transfers stay out of income and spending totals.
- Plaid Link in Sandbox or Production, bank reconnection, incremental transaction syncing, and background sync status. Plaid credentials are saved on the server and redacted from API responses.
- Persistent subscriptions with cadence, next payment, billing channel, management links, notes, and cancellation state. Recurring charges become review candidates when uncertain; known subscription price changes get a separate review.
- Monthly subscription reconciliation that counts actual payments and remaining expected commitments without counting both for the same due payment.
- Cancellation requests queued for a local Codex Luna worker. Jobs pause for login or other user action; completion requires provider text, URL, date, and a matching browser receipt. Sending a request alone never marks a subscription canceled.
- Net worth and investment scenarios with adjustable savings, contributions, returns, inflation, horizon, and debt assumptions. These are illustrations, not forecasts of actual market performance.
- Category budgets, savings goals and contributions, personal/business views, transaction search and notes, CSV export, account archive and restore.
- Reports with a calendar-year selector, all 12 monthly spending totals, yearly and all-time recorded spending, and personal/business filters. Historical reports include archived accounts and exclude pending charges and transfers. Category detail, recent heatmap, and income sources remain available below the overview.
- Purchase lookup for unclear Amazon, Apple and Google charges, using a separate local Codex receipt worker. Verified items can be allocated across category budgets without duplicating the bank charge. Original bank descriptions and manual choices are retained, with review and undo controls in Transactions. Automatic lookups are off until enabled in Settings after setup.
- Single-owner login, private deployment, scheduled syncing, and an encrypted backup utility.

## Home lab installation

See [the Ubuntu and Docker guide](docs/INSTALL.md). The Docker deployment runs as a non-root user with persistent data and publishes only to host loopback. Tailscale Serve or an SSH forward provides private access from other devices.

Plaid production access and your own credentials are required for real banks. Enter credentials in Ledger Settings after signing in. OAuth bank flows also need the private HTTPS return URL registered in your Plaid dashboard.

The optional cancellation worker uses a ChatGPT-authenticated Codex CLI and requests `gpt-5.6-luna`; it rejects API-key login. Model access and usage limits follow your account. Provider login, MFA, CAPTCHA, phone-only cancellation, or account-specific terms can require your involvement. The Docker browser is headless; a visible browser handoff requires the documented GUI worker setup.

## Validation and boundaries

Run isolated checks with:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Bank responses and model execution in tests are mocked. Live production bank linking and subscription cancellation require your account setup and have not been used as tests. Projection history is reconstructed from balances and transactions; it does not include historical market prices or holding-level performance.

Purchase lookup also needs merchant sign-in in the worker's dedicated browser profile. Signing in to Amazon, Apple or Google in the Ledger app's browser does not sign in the worker. Unmatched, grouped or partially funded orders can require review. Receipt lookup does not access email, make purchases, request refunds, or cancel orders. Live merchant receipt retrieval requires setup and has not been used as a test.

Source files and generated releases exclude databases, bank secrets, browser profiles, and Codex login credentials. The app requires its server; it is not a standalone offline phone app.
````````````

### Source: `backend/analytics.py`

<!-- LEDGER_SOURCE {"path":"backend/analytics.py","bytes":13332,"sha256":"973372bae00ecde7b35a98e06b9ec4370c5f876a178b402d80f46b505b75ae95","encoding":"utf-8","mode":"644"} -->
````````````text
"""Analytics: summaries, budgets, recurring detection, reports.

Measured totals come from SQLite; historical net worth is reconstructed, not a balance snapshot.
"""
import calendar
from collections import defaultdict
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

from db import q, q1, month_bounds
import receipt_store


def month_list(n):
    """Last n months as (year, month) tuples ending this month."""
    out = []
    d = date.today()
    y, m = d.year, d.month
    for _ in range(n):
        out.append((y, m))
        m -= 1
        if m == 0:
            y -= 1
            m = 12
    return list(reversed(out))


def mbounds(y, m):
    return date(y, m, 1).isoformat(), date(y + (m == 12), (m % 12) + 1, 1).isoformat()


def _flows(where="1=1", args=()):
    row = q1(
        f"""SELECT
             COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN amount>0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS income,
             COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN amount<0 THEN -amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS spend
           FROM transactions WHERE pending=0 AND is_transfer=0 AND posted<=date('now','localtime') AND {where}""",
        args,
    )
    return row


# ---------------- overview ----------------

def overview(scope=None):
    """scope None => combined; else 'business' or 'personal'."""
    sc = "AND scope=?" if scope else ""
    args = (scope,) if scope else ()
    now_s, now_e = month_bounds()
    py, pm = month_list(2)[0]
    prev_s, prev_e = mbounds(py, pm)

    cur = _flows(f"posted>=? AND posted<? {sc}", (*[now_s, now_e], *args))
    prv = _flows(f"posted>=? AND posted<? {sc}", (*[prev_s, prev_e], *args))

    bal = q1(
        f"SELECT COALESCE(SUM(balance),0) b FROM accounts WHERE archived=0 {'AND scope=?' if scope else ''}",
        args,
    )["b"]

    net_now = cur["income"] - cur["spend"]
    net_prev = prv["income"] - prv["spend"]
    return {
        "net_worth": round(bal, 2),
        "income_this_month": round(cur["income"], 2),
        "spend_this_month": round(cur["spend"], 2),
        "net_this_month": round(net_now, 2),
        "prev_net": round(net_prev, 2),
        "savings_rate": round(net_now / cur["income"], 4) if cur["income"] else None,
        "runway_months": (
            round(bal / cur["spend"], 1)
            if cur["spend"] > 0 and scope != "business"
            else None
        ),
    }


def net_worth_series(months=12, scope=None):
    """End-of-month balance per account type, reconstructed from current
    balances minus transaction flows since each month end."""
    rows = q("SELECT id, balance FROM accounts WHERE archived=0" + (" AND scope=?" if scope else ""), (scope,) if scope else ())
    total_bal = sum(r["balance"] for r in rows)
    tx = q(
        "SELECT posted, SUM(amount) a FROM transactions WHERE pending=0 AND is_transfer=0 AND posted<=date('now','localtime') "
        + ("AND scope=?" if scope else "")
        + " GROUP BY posted",
        (scope,) if scope else (),
    )
    by_day = defaultdict(float)
    for t in tx:
        by_day[t["posted"]] += t["a"]
    out = []
    for y, m in month_list(months):
        eom = date(y + (m == 12), (m % 12) + 1, 1).isoformat()  # first of next month
        future_flow = sum(a for d, a in by_day.items() if d >= eom)
        out.append({"month": f"{y}-{m:02d}", "balance": round(total_bal - future_flow, 2)})
    out[-1]["balance"] = round(total_bal, 2)
    return out


def cashflow_series(months=8, scope=None):
    sc = "AND scope=?" if scope else ""
    args = (scope,) if scope else ()
    out = []
    for y, m in month_list(months):
        s, e = mbounds(y, m)
        f = _flows(f"posted>=? AND posted<? {sc}", (s, e, *args))
        out.append({
            "month": f"{y}-{m:02d}",
            "label": calendar.month_abbr[m],
            "income": round(f["income"], 2),
            "spend": round(f["spend"], 2),
            "net": round(f["income"] - f["spend"], 2),
        })
    return out


def category_breakdown(scope=None, days=90, kind="expense"):
    since = (date.today() - timedelta(days=days)).isoformat()
    sign = "< 0" if kind == "expense" else "> 0"
    txs = q(f"""SELECT t.id,t.amount,t.category_id,COALESCE(c.name,'Uncategorized') name,
                       COALESCE(c.icon,'\U0001F4DD') icon,COALESCE(c.tax_deductible,0) td
                FROM transactions t LEFT JOIN categories c ON t.category_id=c.id
                WHERE t.pending=0 AND t.is_transfer=0 AND t.amount{sign} AND t.posted>=? AND t.posted<=date('now','localtime') {'AND t.scope=?' if scope else ''}""",
             (since, scope) if scope else (since,))
    amap = receipt_store.allocation_map([t["id"] for t in txs]) if kind == "expense" else {}
    grouped = {}
    for tx in txs:
        allocations = amap.get(tx["id"]) or [{"amount_cents": int(round(abs(tx["amount"]) * 100)), "category_id": tx["category_id"], "cat_name": tx["name"]}]
        for allocation in allocations:
            cid = allocation.get("category_id")
            cat = q1("SELECT name,icon,tax_deductible FROM categories WHERE id=?", (cid,)) if cid else None
            key = cid, (cat["name"] if cat else allocation.get("cat_name") or "Uncategorized")
            row = grouped.setdefault(key, {"name": key[1], "icon": (cat or {}).get("icon") or tx["icon"], "td": (cat or {}).get("tax_deductible", tx["td"]), "amt": 0, "n": 0})
            row["amt"] += allocation["amount_cents"] / 100
            row["n"] += 1
    rows = sorted(grouped.values(), key=lambda row: -row["amt"])
    tot = sum(r["amt"] for r in rows) or 1
    for r in rows:
        r["pct"] = round(r["amt"] / tot * 100, 1)
        r["amt"] = round(r["amt"], 2)
    return rows


# ---------------- budgets ----------------

def budget_status():
    s, e = month_bounds()
    budgets = q("""SELECT b.*, c.name cat_name, c.icon cat_icon
                   FROM budgets b LEFT JOIN categories c ON b.category_id=c.id""")
    out = []
    for b in budgets:
        w = "scope=?" if b["scope"] != "all" else "1=1"
        txs = q(
            f"SELECT id,amount,category_id FROM transactions WHERE pending=0 AND is_transfer=0 AND posted<=date('now','localtime') AND amount<0 AND posted>=? AND posted<? AND {w}",
            (s, e, b["scope"]) if b["scope"] != "all" else (s, e),
        )
        amap = receipt_store.allocation_map([t["id"] for t in txs])
        spent = 0
        for tx in txs:
            allocations = amap.get(tx["id"]) or [{"amount_cents": int(round(abs(tx["amount"]) * 100)), "category_id": tx["category_id"]}]
            spent += sum(a["amount_cents"] for a in allocations if a.get("category_id") == b["category_id"]) / 100
        out.append({
            **b,
            "spent": round(spent, 2),
            "pct": round(spent / b["month_limit"] * 100, 1) if b["month_limit"] else 0,
            "remaining": round(b["month_limit"] - spent, 2),
        })
    out.sort(key=lambda x: -x["pct"])
    return out


# ---------------- recurring detection ----------------

def detect_recurring():
    """Group normalized merchant names; flag those appearing >=3 months with similar amounts."""
    rows = q(
        """SELECT merchant, name, amount, posted, scope, category_id
           FROM transactions WHERE amount<0"""
    )
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for t in rows:
        key = (t["merchant"] or t["name"]).lower().strip()[:28]
        groups[key].append(t)
    out = []
    today = date.today()
    for key, ts in groups.items():
        if len(ts) < 3:
            continue
        months = sorted({t["posted"][:7] for t in ts})
        # distinct recent months span
        span = len({m for m in months})
        amounts = [-t["amount"] for t in ts]
        avg = sum(amounts) / len(amounts)
        spread = (max(amounts) - min(amounts)) / avg if avg else 1
        recent = any(t["posted"] >= (today - timedelta(days=45)).isoformat() for t in ts)
        if span >= 3 and spread < 0.35 and recent:
            out.append({
                "merchant": ts[0]["merchant"] or ts[0]["name"],
                "avg_amount": round(avg, 2),
                "last_amount": round(amounts[0], 2),
                "times": len(ts),
                "months_seen": len(months),
                "scope": ts[0]["scope"],
                "category_id": ts[0]["category_id"],
                "monthly_cost": round(avg, 2),
            })
    out.sort(key=lambda x: -x["monthly_cost"])
    return out


def subscriptions_summary():
    import subscriptions
    return subscriptions.listing()


# ---------------- goals & business extras ----------------

def goal_projections():
    goals = q("SELECT * FROM goals ORDER BY completed_at IS NOT NULL, target_date IS NULL, target_date")
    out = []
    today = date.today()
    for g in goals:
        g = dict(g)
        remaining = max(g["target"] - g["saved"], 0)
        eta = None
        if g.get("monthly_plan") and g["monthly_plan"] > 0 and remaining > 0:
            months_left = remaining / g["monthly_plan"]
            eta_y, extra = divmod(int(today.month - 1 + round(months_left)), 12)
            eta_year = today.year + eta_y
            try:
                eta = date(eta_year, int(extra) + 1, 1).isoformat()
            except ValueError:
                eta = None
        on_track = bool(g["target_date"]) and (remaining == 0 or (eta is not None and eta <= g["target_date"]))
        out.append({**g, "remaining": round(remaining, 2), "eta": eta,
                    "on_track": on_track if g.get("target_date") else None,
                    "pct": round(min(g["saved"] / g["target"] * 100, 100), 1) if g["target"] else 0})
    return out


def business_summary():
    ov = overview("business")
    cats = category_breakdown("business", days=365, kind="expense")
    deductible = sum(c["amt"] for c in cats if c["td"])
    inc_rows = q(
        """SELECT COALESCE(c.name,'Other') name, SUM(t.amount) amt, COUNT(*) n
           FROM transactions t LEFT JOIN categories c ON t.category_id=c.id
           WHERE t.pending=0 AND t.is_transfer=0 AND t.posted<=date('now','localtime') AND t.scope='business' AND t.amount>0 AND t.posted>=?
           GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY amt DESC""",
        ((date.today() - timedelta(days=365)).isoformat(),),
    )
    cfg = q1("SELECT tax_rate_business FROM (SELECT ? tax_rate_business)", (_tax_rate(),))
    profit_ytd = sum(r["amt"] for r in inc_rows) - sum(c["amt"] for c in cats)
    top_clients = q(
        """SELECT name, COUNT(*) n, SUM(amount) amt FROM transactions
           WHERE pending=0 AND is_transfer=0 AND posted<=date('now','localtime') AND posted>=date('now','localtime','-365 days') AND scope='business' AND amount>0 GROUP BY name ORDER BY amt DESC LIMIT 5"""
    )
    return {
        "overview": ov,
        "expense_categories_12mo": cats,
        "deductible_12mo": round(deductible, 2),
        "income_sources_12mo": [{"name": r["name"], "amt": round(r["amt"], 2), "n": r["n"]} for r in inc_rows],
        "estimated_tax_setaside": round(max(profit_ytd, 0) * cfg["tax_rate_business"], 2),
        "profit_ttm": round(profit_ytd, 2),
        "top_clients": [{"name": r["name"], "n": r["n"], "amt": round(r["amt"], 2)} for r in top_clients],
    }


def _tax_rate():
    from db import get_config
    return get_config().get("tax_rate_business", 0.253)


def heatmap_data(scope=None, weeks=26):
    since = (date.today() - timedelta(weeks=weeks)).isoformat()
    rows = q(
        f"SELECT posted, SUM(-amount) v FROM transactions WHERE pending=0 AND is_transfer=0 AND posted<=date('now','localtime') AND amount<0 AND posted>=? {'AND scope=?' if scope else ''} GROUP BY posted",
        (since, scope) if scope else (since,),
    )
    return {r["posted"]: round(r["v"], 2) for r in rows}


def monthly_matrix(scope=None, months=6):
    """Category x month spend matrix for reports page."""
    cats = q(
        f"""SELECT DISTINCT COALESCE(c.name,'Uncategorized') name
            FROM transactions t LEFT JOIN categories c ON t.category_id=c.id
            WHERE t.pending=0 AND t.is_transfer=0 AND t.posted<=date('now','localtime') AND t.amount<0 {'AND t.scope=?' if scope else ''}""",
        (scope,) if scope else (),
    )
    names = [c["name"] for c in cats]
    series_out = {}
    for y, m in month_list(months):
        s, e = mbounds(y, m)
        rows = q(
            f"""SELECT t.id,t.amount,t.category_id,COALESCE(c.name,'Uncategorized') name
                FROM transactions t LEFT JOIN categories c ON t.category_id=c.id
                WHERE t.pending=0 AND t.is_transfer=0 AND t.posted<=date('now','localtime') AND t.amount<0 AND t.posted>=? AND t.posted<? {'AND t.scope=?' if scope else ''}
                """,
            (s, e, scope) if scope else (s, e),
        )
        amap = receipt_store.allocation_map([r["id"] for r in rows])
        monthly = defaultdict(float)
        for r in rows:
            allocations = amap.get(r["id"]) or [{"amount_cents": int(round(abs(r["amount"]) * 100)), "cat_name": r["name"]}]
            for allocation in allocations:
                monthly[allocation.get("cat_name") or "Uncategorized"] += allocation["amount_cents"] / 100
        for name, amount in monthly.items():
            series_out.setdefault(name, {})[f"{y}-{m:02d}"] = round(amount, 2)
    names = sorted(set(names) | set(series_out))
    return {"categories": names, "series": series_out}
````````````

````````````text
"""Single-owner authentication for the local Ledger service.

The module intentionally has no dependency on the HTTP server.  It stores a
password verifier and hashes of random bearer session tokens in SQLite.  The
server owns cookie, origin, and request plumbing; callers only need the small
public interface in ``docs/INTERFACES.md``.
"""

import base64
import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import sqlite3
import time
import re
from datetime import datetime, timezone

try:  # ``python backend/server.py`` puts backend/ on sys.path.
    import db
except ImportError:  # package imports used by the test suite.
    from . import db


SESSION_TTL = 12 * 60 * 60
MAX_FAILURES = 5
RATE_WINDOW = 15 * 60
LOCKOUT_SECONDS = 15 * 60
PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = 12
TOKEN_BYTES = 32
MAX_SESSION_TTL = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60


def _now():
    return time.time()


def _utc(ts=None):
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(_now() if ts is None else ts, timezone.utc).isoformat()


def _token_hash(token):
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _session_ttl(value):
    try:
        value = int(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        raise ValueError("session lifetime must be a number")
    if value <= 0 or value > MAX_SESSION_TTL:
        raise ValueError("session lifetime is outside the allowed range")
    return value


def _password_hash(password, salt=None):
    """Return a portable verifier string and salt.

    scrypt is preferred and available in supported CPython builds.  PBKDF2 is
    retained as a standard-library fallback for constrained Python builds.
    """
    if not isinstance(password, str):
        raise ValueError("password must be text")
    if len(password) < PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH:
        raise ValueError(f"password must be at least {PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH} characters")
    salt = salt or secrets.token_bytes(16)
    try:
        value = hashlib.scrypt(password.encode("utf-8"), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
        return "scrypt$16384$8$1$" + _b64(salt) + "$" + _b64(value), salt
    except (AttributeError, ValueError):
        value = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", password.encode("utf-8"), salt, 600_000)
        return "pbkdf2-sha256$600000$" + _b64(salt) + "$" + _b64(value), salt


def _verify_password(password, encoded):
    try:
        if not isinstance(password, str) or not isinstance(encoded, str):
            return False
        parts = encoded.split("$")
        if parts[0] == "scrypt" and len(parts) == 6:
            _, n, r, p, salt_s, value_s = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3], parts[4], parts[5]
            salt, expected = _unb64(salt_s), _unb64(value_s)
            actual = hashlib.scrypt(password.encode("utf-8"), salt=salt,
                                    n=int(n), r=int(r), p=int(p), maxmem=64 * 1024 * 1024)
        elif parts[0] == "pbkdf2-sha256" and len(parts) == 4:
            _, iterations, salt_s, value_s = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], parts[3]
            salt, expected = _unb64(salt_s), _unb64(value_s)
            actual = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", password.encode("utf-8"), salt,
                                        int(iterations))
        else:
            return False
        return hmac.compare_digest(actual, expected)
    except (TypeError, ValueError, IndexError, OverflowError):
        return False


def _b64(value):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(value).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")


def _unb64(value):
    return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(value + "=" * (-len(value) % 4))


def init_schema():
    """Create auth tables and indexes. Safe to call during every startup."""
    c = db._conn()
    c.executescript("""
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_owner (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
        password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
        password_salt TEXT NOT NULL,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
      );
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_sessions (
        token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        expires_at REAL NOT NULL,
        last_seen_at TEXT NOT NULL,
        remote_addr TEXT,
        revoked_at TEXT
      );
      CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_auth_sessions_expiry ON auth_sessions(expires_at);
      CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auth_login_limits (
        remote_addr TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
        window_started REAL NOT NULL,
        failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        blocked_until REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
      );
    """)
    c.commit()
    c.close()


def configured():
    init_schema()
    return bool(db.q1("SELECT 1 FROM auth_owner WHERE id=1"))


def _new_session(remote="", session_ttl=SESSION_TTL):
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(TOKEN_BYTES)
    now = _now()
    session_ttl = _session_ttl(session_ttl)
    remote = remote if isinstance(remote, str) else ""
    db.ex("INSERT INTO auth_sessions(token_hash,created_at,expires_at,last_seen_at,remote_addr,revoked_at) "
          "VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,NULL)",
          (_token_hash(token), _utc(now), now + session_ttl, _utc(now), remote[:255],))
    return token


def setup(password, remote="", session_ttl=SESSION_TTL):
    """Set up the one owner and return a newly authenticated session token.

    Setup is intentionally one-shot.  The HTTP layer must enforce localhost
    for this operation; the module does not guess whether an address is safe.
    """
    init_schema()
    if configured():
        raise ValueError("owner is already configured")
    # Validate optional test/deployment overrides before committing the owner,
    # so an invalid lifetime cannot leave a half-configured installation.
    session_ttl = _session_ttl(session_ttl)
    encoded, salt = _password_hash(password)
    now = _utc()
    c = db._conn()
    try:
        c.execute("INSERT INTO auth_owner VALUES(1,?,?,?,?)", (encoded, _b64(salt), now, now))
        c.commit()
    except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
        c.rollback()
        raise ValueError("owner is already configured")
    finally:
        c.close()
    return _new_session(remote, session_ttl)


def _rate_state(remote):
    key = (remote or "unknown")[:255]
    row = db.q1("SELECT * FROM auth_login_limits WHERE remote_addr=?", (key,))
    now = _now()
    if not row or now - row["window_started"] >= RATE_WINDOW:
        db.ex("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO auth_login_limits(remote_addr,window_started,failures,blocked_until) VALUES(?,?,0,0)",
              (key, now))
        return key, now, 0, 0
    return key, row["window_started"], row["failures"], row["blocked_until"]


def _record_failure(remote):
    key, started, failures, blocked = _rate_state(remote)
    failures += 1
    blocked = max(blocked, _now() + LOCKOUT_SECONDS) if failures >= MAX_FAILURES else blocked
    db.ex("UPDATE auth_login_limits SET failures=?,blocked_until=? WHERE remote_addr=?",
          (failures, blocked, key))


def _clear_failures(remote):
    key = (remote or "unknown")[:255]
    db.ex("DELETE FROM auth_login_limits WHERE remote_addr=?", (key,))


def login(password, remote="", session_ttl=SESSION_TTL):
    """Verify the owner password and return a random session token.

    All failure cases intentionally share ``ValueError`` so callers cannot
    distinguish an unconfigured owner, bad password, or temporary lockout.
    """
    init_schema()
    row = db.q1("SELECT password_hash FROM auth_owner WHERE id=1")
    # Run a verifier even before setup to keep the path less distinguishable.
    if not row:
        _password_hash("Ledger unavailable: placeholder password")
        raise ValueError("authentication unavailable")
    key, _, _, blocked_until = _rate_state(remote)
    if _now() < blocked_until:
        raise ValueError("too many login attempts; try again later")
    if not isinstance(password, str) or not _verify_password(password, row["password_hash"]):
        _record_failure(key)
        raise ValueError("invalid credentials")
    _clear_failures(key)
    return _new_session(remote, session_ttl)


def validate(token):
    """Return whether a session token is active and unexpired."""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > 512:
        return False
    init_schema()
    row = db.q1("SELECT expires_at,revoked_at FROM auth_sessions WHERE token_hash=?", (_token_hash(token),))
    if not row or row["revoked_at"] or _now() >= row["expires_at"]:
        if row and _now() >= row["expires_at"]:
            db.ex("DELETE FROM auth_sessions WHERE token_hash=?", (_token_hash(token),))
        return False
    db.ex("UPDATE auth_sessions SET last_seen_at=? WHERE token_hash=?", (_utc(), _token_hash(token)))
    return True


def logout(token):
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token or len(token) > 512:
        return
    init_schema()
    db.ex("UPDATE auth_sessions SET revoked_at=? WHERE token_hash=? AND revoked_at IS NULL", (_utc(), _token_hash(token)))


def cleanup_sessions():
    """Remove expired and revoked sessions; useful for a periodic maintenance task."""
    init_schema()
    db.ex("DELETE FROM auth_sessions WHERE expires_at<=? OR revoked_at IS NOT NULL", (_now(),))


def token_from_cookie(cookie_header, cookie_name="ledger_session"):
    """Extract one cookie value without exposing other cookie contents."""
    if not cookie_header:
        return None
    for part in cookie_header.split(";"):
        name, sep, value = part.strip().partition("=")
        if sep and name == cookie_name:
            return value or None
    return None


def make_session_cookie(token, secure=False, max_age=SESSION_TTL, cookie_name="ledger_session"):
    """Build a restrictive Set-Cookie value for the server's response layer."""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]+", token):
        raise ValueError("token required")
    attrs = [f"{cookie_name}={token}", "Path=/", "HttpOnly", "SameSite=Strict", f"Max-Age={int(max_age)}"]
    if secure:
        attrs.append("Secure")
    return "; ".join(attrs)
````````````
